modules.gx: Lower-level graphics API exposing triangle/line submission, explicit flat shade, culling, depth, matrices, and raw buffer access. Shares the framebuffer, camera, and model transform with egx. Shapes, text, OBJ loading, input, and lights belong to egx.
modules.egx: Easy GX: convenient shapes, text, camera setup, OBJ models, lighting, scenes, and input. Works on its own. Mix with gx for explicit primitives; both share the framebuffer, native camera, model transform, and depth buffer.
modules.py5: Python-style drawing facade with fill/stroke settings, shape construction, and geometry transforms. TiPy supports the listed subset; this is not the full desktop py5 library.
modules.time: Calculator timing functions for blocking sleep and a wrapping 128 Hz frame-tick counter.
modules.random: Native pseudorandom integer generation and explicit seeding for repeatable sequences.
modules.math: Supported native angle conversion, sine, and cosine functions. Trigonometric angles are in radians.
modules.timing: Optional TiPy helper module containing Clock for elapsed milliseconds and frame-rate limiting.
modules.motion: Optional TiPy helper module containing heading() and FirstPerson movement with fractional positions and collision sliding.
modules.geometry: Optional TiPy helper module containing mutable integer Vector2 and Rect classes.
modules.lighting: Optional TiPy helper module containing OrbitLight for animating a point-light position.

functions.abs: Returns the absolute value of a number. The result must fit its TiPy numeric type.
functions.all: Returns True if every element is truthy. Returns True for an empty iterable.
functions.any: Returns True if at least one element is truthy. Returns False for an empty iterable.
functions.bool: Converts a value to True or False using TiPy's truth-value rules.
functions.dict: Creates an empty dictionary. Its key and value types must be established by context or subsequent use.
functions.divmod: Returns a tuple containing the floor-division quotient and remainder of a and b. A zero divisor raises an error.
functions.enumerate: Iterates over (index, value) pairs. The index starts at zero unless a start argument is supplied.
functions.filter: Returns an iterator over values for which the supplied predicate is truthy. A None predicate tests each value itself.
functions.float: Converts a numeric value to TiPy's float type.
functions.int: Converts a value to a signed 16-bit integer. int is an alias for i16, with range -32768 through 32767.
functions.iter: Returns an iterator over an iterable. Use next() to consume its elements one at a time.
functions.len: Returns the number of elements in a collection or characters in a string. Container lengths are stored, so this does not scan the elements.
functions.list: Builds a new mutable, typed list from an iterable, such as list(range(30)). List storage uses the program heap.
functions.map: Returns an iterator that calls the supplied function for each element of an iterable and yields the results.
functions.max: Returns the greatest of its arguments, or the greatest element of a single iterable. An empty iterable raises an error.
functions.min: Returns the least of its arguments, or the least element of a single iterable. An empty iterable raises an error.
functions.next: Consumes and returns the next iterator value. At exhaustion, returns the optional default or raises StopIteration.
functions.pow: Raises base to exponent. The optional third integer argument computes the result modulo that argument.
functions.range: Produces an integer sequence with an excluded stop value. Forms: range(stop), range(start, stop), and range(start, stop, step). A negative step counts down; step cannot be zero.
functions.reversed: Returns an iterator over an indexed sequence in reverse order without reversing the original sequence.
functions.round: Rounds a number, optionally to a specified number of decimal places. Returns an integer when decimal places are omitted.
functions.set: Builds a typed collection of unique elements from an iterable. Duplicate elements are discarded.
functions.sorted: Returns a new sorted list, leaving the original iterable unchanged. Use reverse=True for descending order.
functions.str: Converts a supported value to text. Use the returned string with print() or string operations.
functions.sum: Adds the elements of a numeric iterable and returns the total. An optional start value is added first.
functions.tuple: Builds an immutable tuple from an iterable. Tuple element types are tracked by the compiler.
functions.zip: Iterates over tuples containing one element from each input iterable. Stops when the shortest input is exhausted.
functions.clear: Clears the drawing buffer to white. Call render() to show the cleared buffer on the 96 x 64 screen.
functions.render: Copies the drawing buffer to the calculator LCD. Drawing commands change the buffer; render() makes those changes visible.
functions.clear_rect: Erases a screen-space rectangle to white. x and y are its top-left pixel; width and height are pixel counts. The rectangle is clipped to the screen.
functions.pixel_on: Sets the pixel at (x, y) to black in the drawing buffer. Screen coordinates start at the top-left: x=0..95 and y=0..63. Out-of-bounds pixels are ignored. Call render() to display the change.
functions.pixel_off: Clears the pixel at (x, y) to white in the drawing buffer. Out-of-bounds pixels are ignored. Call render() to display the change.
functions.flip_pixel: Toggles the pixel at (x, y) between black and white in the drawing buffer. Out-of-bounds pixels are ignored. Call render() to display the change.
functions.key_down: Returns True while the named calculator key is held, so it can be polled every frame. Examples: "left", "right", "up", "down", "2nd", "enter", and "clear". In the emulator, click the screen for keyboard focus; Ctrl is 2nd and Escape is Clear.
functions.print: Draws text, an integer, or a bool at the top-left pixel position (x, y), using a 5 x 7 font with six-pixel character spacing. Glyph pixels are added over the existing image without erasing a background rectangle. Call render() to display the result.
functions.input: Draws a prompt at pixel position (x, y), then waits for editable input with a blinking cursor. Enter submits. Assign to an int variable for signed-integer input, or a str variable for text input. This renders while waiting; leave enough screen space after the prompt for the text and cursor.
functions.line: Draws a line between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), clipped to the screen. The six-coordinate overload draws an XYZ line through the configured camera. Call render() to display it.
functions.h_line: Draws an inclusive horizontal line from x1 to x2 at y1. y1 and y2 must match; otherwise nothing is drawn. The line is clipped to the screen.
functions.v_line: Draws an inclusive vertical line from y1 to y2 at x1. x1 and x2 must match; otherwise nothing is drawn. The line is clipped to the screen.
functions.rectangle: Draws a rectangle using inclusive corner coordinates in the order (x1, x2, y1, y2). width is border thickness, not the rectangle's horizontal size. filled=True fills the interior; False draws the border.
functions.rect: Draws a rectangle at top-left (x, y) with the supplied width and height, using the current fill and stroke settings.
functions.circle: Draws a circle centered at (x, y), with the supplied diameter in pixels, using the current fill and stroke settings. For an EGX circle specified by radius, use draw_circle().
functions.ellipse: Draws an ellipse centered at (x, y) with the supplied full width and height in pixels, using the current fill and stroke settings.
functions.triangle: Draws a triangle through three XY vertices using the current fill and stroke settings.
functions.quad: Draws a quadrilateral through four XY vertices in boundary order, using the current fill and stroke settings.
functions.polygon: Draws a closed polygon from a list of (x, y) points, using the current fill and stroke settings.
functions.polyline: Draws connected segments through a list of (x, y) points. The closed argument controls whether the final point connects back to the first.
functions.point: Draws a point using the current stroke settings. The two-coordinate form is XY; the three-coordinate form is XYZ and uses the configured camera.
functions.background: Fills the entire drawing buffer with the supplied grayscale color, using monochrome dithering for intermediate shades. Call render() to display it.
functions.fill: Enables filled interiors for subsequent styled shapes and selects their grayscale color: 0 is black and 255 is white. Intermediate shades use 1-bit dithering.
functions.no_fill: Disables filled interiors for subsequent styled shapes. Their outlines still depend on the current stroke setting.
functions.stroke: Enables outlines for subsequent styled shapes and selects their grayscale color: 0 is black and 255 is white.
functions.no_stroke: Disables outlines for subsequent styled shapes. Their interiors still depend on the current fill setting.
functions.stroke_weight: Sets the thickness, in pixels, of strokes used by subsequent styled drawing commands.
functions.begin_shape: Starts a custom shape and clears its accumulated vertices. Add vertices with vertex(), then finish with end_shape().
functions.vertex: Adds an XY or XYZ vertex to the custom shape started by begin_shape(). XYZ vertices are projected through the camera.
functions.end_shape: Draws the vertices collected since begin_shape(), using current fill and stroke settings. Pass True or py5.CLOSE to close the boundary; False or py5.OPEN leaves it open.
functions.translate: Offsets subsequent geometry by x and y, with optional z. Transform changes accumulate until reset_matrix() or pop_matrix().
functions.scale: Scales subsequent geometry. The py5-style API accepts one uniform factor or separate axis factors. GX and EGX accept one positive uniform factor.
functions.rotate: Rotates subsequent geometry around the Z axis by an angle in radians. In XY drawing, this rotates around the current origin.
functions.rotate_x: Rotates subsequent geometry around the X axis by an angle in radians.
functions.rotate_y: Rotates subsequent geometry around the Y axis by an angle in radians.
functions.rotate_z: Rotates subsequent geometry around the Z axis by an angle in radians.
functions.push_matrix: Saves the current geometry transform so it can be restored with pop_matrix(). In GX and EGX the shared stack holds up to eight saved transforms. This does not save fill, stroke, lights, or the camera.
functions.pop_matrix: Restores the most recently saved geometry transform and removes it from the stack. Pair it with push_matrix(); popping an empty GX/EGX stack raises a runtime error.
functions.reset_matrix: Restores the identity geometry transform, removing accumulated translation, rotation, and scaling. The camera and drawing styles are unchanged.
functions.apply_matrix: Multiplies the current geometry transform by the supplied 4 x 4 matrix, given as sixteen values. Subsequent geometry uses the combined transform.
functions.init_camera: Configures perspective projection for XYZ drawing. fov is the field of view in degrees; near and far are clipping distances. Screen-space XY drawing is independent of the camera.
functions.camera: Places the camera at (eye_x, eye_y, eye_z) and aims it toward (target_x, target_y, target_z). It affects XYZ geometry, while screen-space XY drawing stays independent. coordinate_scale can specify fractional coordinate units in the native mesh path.
functions.set_fov: Changes the perspective camera's field of view in degrees. Smaller values zoom in; larger values show a wider view.
functions.mesh: Creates a static mesh from literal XYZ vertices and edge or triangle-face index lists. Returns a model handle for draw_mesh(). Supports at most 64 vertices, 192 edges, and 128 faces; supply edges or faces.
functions.load_obj: Loads a project OBJ asset at compile time and returns a model handle. object selects a named OBJ object. normalize=True scales the model to radius (1..59); False preserves its coordinates. brightness is a constant in 0..16. Keep the OBJ beside the entry .tip file.
functions.draw_mesh: Transforms and projects a mesh handle into the drawing buffer. Position, rotation, size, face filling, culling, lighting, depth testing, and outlines can be controlled independently. Call render() to display it.
functions.draw_shadow: Projects a mesh's simple shadow from a point-light position onto the horizontal plane floor_y. x, y, and z place the model; max_distance bounds shadow reach. Draw the shadow with the scene before render().
functions.collision_map: Creates a collision-map handle from a project OBJ's collision geometry, or supported literal collision boxes. Test proposed XZ positions with collides().
functions.collides: Returns True when an XZ position and radius intersect the supplied collision map. coordinate_scale can express positions in fractional world units. This tests a position; it does not move or slide an object.
functions.mesh_light: Sets the mesh renderer's basic light direction (x, y, z) and ambient brightness. Used for shading filled mesh faces.
functions.no_lights: Clears the configured mesh lights. Add ambient, directional, or point lighting afterward to define lighting for the next draws.
functions.ambient_light: Sets uniform mesh illumination, independent of face direction or distance. level uses the renderer's 0..16 brightness scale.
functions.directional_light: Adds a directional mesh light with vector (x, y, z). Its intensity does not decay with distance. intensity uses the renderer's 0..16 scale; filled shaded faces use 1-bit dithering.
functions.point_light: Adds a mesh light at world position (x, y, z). radius controls its distance falloff and intensity controls its strength on a 0..16 scale. Filled shaded faces use 1-bit dithering.
functions.load_scene: Loads named geometry groups from a project OBJ at compile time and returns a scene handle. Options select a background object, floor height, ambient light, per-object brightness, unlit objects, and simple shadows. Keep the OBJ beside the entry .tip file.
functions.draw_scene: Draws a loaded scene's visible geometry in its compiled visibility order. Optional shadow_light=(x, y, z) supplies a point-light position for simple floor shadows. Call render() afterward.
functions.set_visible: Shows or hides the named object in a loaded scene. Later draw_scene() calls use the updated visibility.
functions.scene_collisions: Returns a collision-map handle for a loaded scene. Pass it to collides() to test movement against the scene's collision boxes.
functions.set_cpu_speed: Selects a calculator CPU speed of 6 or 15 MHz. The emulator models the selected clock; compatible TI-84 Plus hardware uses the corresponding speed mode.
functions.set_render_quality: Selects the mesh renderer's approximation policy at compile time. Use one top-level call with "exact" or "aggressive". Aggressive trades some geometric and lighting precision for speed.
functions.time.sleep: Pauses execution for the supplied number of seconds. Supports fractional seconds, from 0 through 32.767; this blocks the program rather than running another drawing frame.
functions.time.frame_ticks: Returns the calculator frame timer's 128 Hz tick counter, which wraps at 256. For elapsed ticks use (now - previous) & 255; a timer tick is not a rendered frame.
functions.time.stop_frame_timer: Stops the frame timer used by time.frame_ticks(), restoring its timer configuration. Call when the program no longer needs frame timing.
functions.random.randint: Returns a pseudorandom integer between low and high, including both endpoints. low must not exceed high.
functions.random.seed: Sets the pseudorandom generator's seed. Reusing a seed reproduces the same subsequent random sequence.
functions.math.radians: Converts an angle in degrees to radians for trigonometric and rotation functions.
functions.math.sin: Returns an approximate sine of an angle in radians, with a result from -1 through 1.
functions.math.cos: Returns an approximate cosine of an angle in radians, with a result from -1 through 1.
functions.init: Starts a graphics session, saves the previous calculator CPU speed, and selects 15 MHz for drawing. Pair with quit() when finished.
functions.quit: Ends the graphics session, restores the saved CPU speed, and stops the frame timer. It does not erase the last rendered image.
functions.flip: Displays the current drawing buffer on the LCD. This is an alias for render(); it does not toggle individual pixels.
functions.draw_line: Draws a line between the two XY endpoints in the drawing buffer. GX/EGX geometry uses their shared model transform. Call render() to display it.
functions.draw_rect: Draws a rectangle at top-left (x, y) with width and height in drawing units. thickness sets border width; filled=True fills the interior and False draws only the border. EGX applies the shared geometry transform.
functions.draw_circle: Draws a circle centered at (x, y) with the supplied radius. filled=True fills the disk; False draws its boundary. EGX applies the shared geometry transform.
functions.draw_text: Draws text, an integer, or a bool at screen-space top-left (x, y), without erasing a background rectangle. This is an alias for print(); geometry transforms do not move the text. Call render() to display it.
functions.get_pixel: Returns whether the screen-space pixel (x, y) is black in the drawing buffer. Reads the buffer rather than the LCD and does not use the model transform.
functions.get_buffer_byte: Reads one byte of the 768-byte screen drawing buffer. Each row has 12 bytes; the most significant bit is the leftmost pixel in a byte. This bypasses geometry transforms.
functions.set_buffer_byte: Writes one byte of the 768-byte screen drawing buffer. Each row has 12 bytes; bit 7 controls the leftmost pixel in a byte. This bypasses geometry transforms; call render() to display the change.
functions.camera_x: Returns the native mesh camera's current world-space X position.
functions.camera_y: Returns the native mesh camera's current world-space Y position.
functions.camera_z: Returns the native mesh camera's current world-space Z position.
functions.load_view_matrix: Loads an explicit native mesh camera position and 3 x 3 view rotation matrix. This bypasses look-at camera calculation; matrix entries use the renderer's Q8.8 fixed-point representation, where 256 represents 1.
functions.set_projection: Configures the native camera's perspective field of view in degrees and its near/far clipping distances. This is the GX alias for init_camera().
functions.mul_fixed: Multiplies two signed Q8.8 fixed-point values and returns a Q8.8 result, equivalent to scaling their product down by 256. In this representation 256 means 1.
functions.CLOSE: True-valued constant passed to end_shape() to connect the final vertex back to the first.
functions.OPEN: False-valued constant passed to end_shape() to leave the final shape boundary open.
functions.begin: Starts an explicit primitive submission with gx.TRIANGLES (independent triples) or gx.LINES (independent pairs). Add XY or XYZ vertices, then call end(). One fixed primitive buffer is reused; nested submissions raise RuntimeError.
functions.gx.vertex: Submits an XY vertex (x,y), or an XYZ world vertex (x,y,z), between begin() and end(). The shared model transform applies at submission. XYZ uses the shared native camera; camera-relative abs(x)+abs(y)+abs(z) must not exceed 120. Every complete triangle or line is rasterized immediately without heap allocation.
functions.end: Ends the current GX submission. An incomplete triangle or line raises RuntimeError and resets submission state; already completed primitives remain drawn. end() does not display the LCD: call render().
functions.draw: Submits a vertex sequence as independent triangles or lines. Optional indices select zero-based vertices. dimensions defaults to 2 (XY); pass dimensions=3 for XYZ. Buffers are read without modification, arguments are evaluated once in source order, and literal constant buffers do not allocate a heap.
functions.shade: Sets the persistent flat GX shade: 0 is black and 255 is white. Triangles use 17 ordered-dither levels. Lines use black below the midpoint and white at or above it. GX does not calculate EGX lighting for these primitives.
functions.depth_test: Enables or disables inverse-depth testing for subsequent filled XYZ GX triangles; defaults to False. XY triangles and lines are overlays that neither test nor write depth. A 6144-byte depth buffer is linked only when needed; clear() resets it.
functions.cull: Enables or disables back-face culling for subsequent GX triangles; defaults to False. Clockwise screen-coordinate faces are front-facing. Lines are unaffected.
functions.load_matrix: Replaces the shared model matrix with sixteen row-major numeric entries. The final affine row must be literal 0,0,0,1; translation is m03,m13,m23. Affects subsequent GX vertices and EGX geometry. Use push_matrix()/pop_matrix() to restore the previous transform.
functions.TRIANGLES: Primitive mode for gx.begin() or gx.draw(): each independent group of three vertices defines one filled triangle.
functions.LINES: Primitive mode for gx.begin() or gx.draw(): each independent pair of vertices defines one line segment. Lines are drawn as overlays without depth testing.

list.append: Adds one value to the end of this list, growing its storage if necessary. Mutates the list and returns no value.
list.insert: Inserts a value before the specified index, shifting later elements. Mutates the list.
list.pop: Removes and returns the element at index. The default index -1 removes the last element. Raises an error for an empty list or invalid index.
list.remove: Removes the first element equal to value. Raises an error if no matching element exists.
list.clear: Removes all elements from this list, making its length zero.
list.extend: Appends the elements of another compatible list to this list, preserving their order.
list.reverse: Reverses the elements in place. Mutates this list rather than making a reversed copy.
list.copy: Returns a new list containing the same elements. This is a shallow copy.
list.count: Returns the number of list elements equal to value.
list.index: Returns the index of the first element equal to value. Raises an error if the value is absent.
list.sort: Sorts this list in place. Use reverse=True for descending order; the method returns no value.

str.upper: Returns a new string with ASCII lowercase letters converted to uppercase.
str.lower: Returns a new string with ASCII uppercase letters converted to lowercase.
str.capitalize: Returns a new string with the first character uppercased and the remaining characters lowercased.
str.title: Returns a new string with words converted to title case using TiPy's character rules.
str.swapcase: Returns a new string with ASCII uppercase and lowercase letters exchanged.
str.join: Returns a string formed by joining a sequence of strings, placing this separator string between adjacent elements.
str.find: Returns the first index of sub within the optional start/end bounds, or -1 if it is absent. The end bound is excluded.
str.rfind: Returns the last index of sub within the optional start/end bounds, or -1 if it is absent. The end bound is excluded.
str.index: Returns the first index of sub within the optional start/end bounds. Raises ValueError if it is absent.
str.rindex: Returns the last index of sub within the optional start/end bounds. Raises ValueError if it is absent.
str.count: Counts non-overlapping occurrences of sub within the optional start/end bounds.
str.startswith: Returns True if the selected portion of this string begins with sub. Optional start/end bounds select that portion.
str.endswith: Returns True if the selected portion of this string ends with sub. Optional start/end bounds select that portion.
str.replace: Returns a new string with old occurrences replaced by new. count limits the number of replacements; -1 replaces all occurrences.
str.split: Returns a list of substrings separated by sep. Omitting sep splits on whitespace. maxsplit limits splits; -1 means no limit.
str.strip: Returns a copy with leading and trailing characters removed. Without chars, removes whitespace; chars is a set of removable characters, not a substring.
str.lstrip: Returns a copy with leading characters removed. Without chars, removes whitespace; chars specifies removable characters.
str.rstrip: Returns a copy with trailing characters removed. Without chars, removes whitespace; chars specifies removable characters.

dict.get: Returns the value for key, or the required default argument if the key is absent. Does not insert the default.
dict.setdefault: Returns the value for key. If absent, inserts the supplied default and returns it.
dict.pop: Removes key and returns its value. An optional default is returned if the key is absent; without a default, a missing key raises KeyError.
dict.clear: Removes every key/value entry from this dictionary.
dict.copy: Returns a new dictionary containing the same entries. This is a shallow copy.
dict.update: Copies entries from another compatible dictionary into this one, replacing values for keys already present.
dict.keys: Returns an iterable view of the dictionary's keys. Changing its size during iteration raises an error.
dict.values: Returns an iterable view of the dictionary's values. Changing its size during iteration raises an error.
dict.items: Returns an iterable view of (key, value) pairs, suitable for for key, value in dictionary.items(). Changing its size during iteration raises an error.

helpers.timing.Clock: Creates a frame clock for measuring elapsed time and optionally limiting frame rate. Pass its tick() result to movement and animation updates.
helpers.timing.Clock.tick: Returns elapsed time in milliseconds since the previous tick. If fps is positive, waits as necessary to limit frame rate. max_ms clamps the returned time after a long frame.
helpers.timing.Clock.tick_ticks: Returns elapsed raw 128 Hz timer ticks since the previous clock update, clamped to maximum. This returns ticks, not milliseconds.
helpers.motion.heading: Returns an integer approximation of sine with amplitude about 128. angle uses 128 steps per full turn; heading(angle + 32) supplies the cosine-like component.
helpers.motion.FirstPerson: Creates a first-person XZ movement controller. x and z are world coordinates, yaw is in degrees, and speed controls movement. Fractional movement and collision handling stay inside the helper.
helpers.motion.FirstPerson.move: Updates movement and turning from forward, strafe, and turn inputs using elapsed dt in milliseconds. walls is a collision-map handle; blocked motion is tested separately on each axis to allow sliding.
helpers.motion.FirstPerson.slide: Tests one proposed axis movement against a collision map using the controller's fractional units. Returns the candidate position if clear, otherwise the original position.
helpers.motion.FirstPerson.look: Updates the shared camera from this controller's current position and heading.
helpers.motion.FirstPerson.near: Returns True if this controller is within the supplied X and Z distance bounds of a world position. This uses an axis-aligned proximity test, not a circular distance.
helpers.geometry.Vector2: Creates a mutable two-component integer vector with public x and y fields.
helpers.geometry.Vector2.move_ip: Adds dx and dy to this vector's x and y fields in place.
helpers.geometry.Vector2.scale_ip: Multiplies this vector's x and y components by the integer amount in place.
helpers.geometry.Vector2.length_squared: Returns x*x + y*y without a square root. Useful for comparing distances while avoiding square-root cost; the result must fit the integer type.
helpers.geometry.Rect: Creates an axis-aligned rectangle with public x, y, width, and height fields. x and y identify its top-left corner.
helpers.geometry.Rect.move_ip: Moves this rectangle by adding dx and dy to its top-left position in place.
helpers.geometry.Rect.collidepoint: Returns True when (x, y) lies inside this rectangle. Left/top edges are included; right/bottom edges are excluded.
helpers.lighting.OrbitLight: Creates an animated point-light position orbiting in the XZ plane. radius and height are world units; period is the full-orbit duration in seconds. Use its x, height, and z fields with point_light().
helpers.lighting.OrbitLight.update: Advances the light's orbit by dt milliseconds and updates its x and z fields. Does not configure or draw a light by itself.
